ImageDescription.value:
The residential building of the Deaconess Institute's block, located at the corner of Alppikatu and Kolmas linja. In the City of Helsinki's Participation and Assessment Plan (OAS), published on March 3, 2025, the city is planning redevelopment of the residential building's site. According to the OAS, the building was completed in 1955 and was designed by architect Eino Tuompo. In the OAS, the building is also listed under the name Alppikulma. The building has nine floors.
Viewing direction west. In the foreground of the image is the intersection of Alppikatu and Kolmas linja.

ImageDescription.value: The Olofsborg apartment house in the Katajanokka neighborhood in Helsinki was built in 1902 and designed by Gesellius, Lindgren, & Saarinen architects.  It is located at Katajanokankatu 1 (Skatuddsgatan 1) / Kauppiaankatu 7 (Köpmansgatan 7). The towers of the building are inspired by the Olavinlinna Castle in Savonlinna, which is called Olofsborg in Swedish. In 2007, Olofsborg was second runner-up in a public vote for the most beautiful Jugendstil (Art Nouveau) building in Helsinki sponsored by the newspaper Helsingin Sanomat.

ImageDescription.value: Standertskjöldin talo (Standertskjöld House), built in 1885, was developed by Carl August Standertskjöld and designed by architect Theodor Höijer. This apartment building is located in the Kruununhaka neighborhood of Helsinki at Pohjoisranta 4 and Kirkkokatu 2. The street names reflect the building’s location along the northern portion of central Helsinki’s waterfront (Pohjoisranta has a meaning similar to North Quay or North Esplanade) and near major churches (Kirkkokatu means church street).
